chunks: 2325 - It has been narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus, who said:

Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ was one of the students of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, then he deviated from tawḥīd. So it was said to him: You abandoned the doctrine of your companion and entered into something that has neither foundation nor reality. He said: My companion was inconsistent; at one time he would speak of qadar, and at another time of jabr, and I do not know him to have held to any doctrine consistently.

He said: He entered Makkah in rebellion and denial against those who perform hajj. The scholars disliked his questioning them and his sitting with them because of the malice of his tongue and the corruption of his inner state. Then he came to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام and sat before him in a group of his peers. He then said to him: Gatherings are trusts, and everyone who has a cough must inevitably cough, so will you permit me to speak? He said: “Speak.” He said: How long will you tread upon this threshing floor, seek refuge with this stone, worship this House raised with brick and clay, and run around it like the running of a camel when it bolts? Whoever reflects upon this or estimates it knows that this is an act founded by one who was neither wise nor possessed of insight. So answer, for you are the head of this matter and its summit, and your father is its foundation and order.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the one whom Allah has led astray and whose heart He has blinded finds the truth distasteful and does not find it sweet. Shayṭān becomes his guardian, bringing him to the watering places of destruction and then never bringing him back. This is a House by which Allah has made His creation worshipful, so that He may test their obedience in coming to it. He urged them to venerate it and visit it, and made it the place of His Prophets and a qiblah for those who perform salat to Him. Thus it is a branch of His good pleasure and a path that leads to His forgiveness, erected upon the levelness of perfection and the meeting place of greatness and majesty. Allah created it two thousand years before the spreading out of the earth, and the One most worthy to be obeyed in what He commands, and to be refrained from regarding what He forbids and warns against, is Allah, the One who brings forth spirits with forms.”

Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ said: You have mentioned, O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and thus referred to one absent. Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Woe to you! How can He be absent when He is present with His creation and is nearer to them than the jugular vein, hearing their speech, seeing their persons, and knowing their secrets?”

“Rather, it is the created being who, when he moves from one place, a place becomes occupied by him and a place becomes empty of him, so in the place to which he has gone he does not know what has occurred in the place where he had been. But as for Allah, tremendous in affair, the Sovereign, the Judge, no place is devoid of Him, no place occupies Him, and He is not nearer to one place than to another. And the one whom He sent with decisive signs and clear proofs, whom He strengthened with His help and chose for conveying His messages—we have affirmed his statement that his Lord sent him and spoke to him.”

Then Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ rose from him and said to his companions: Who cast me into this sea? I asked you to seek for me a shade-mat, but you threw me onto a live ember. They said to him: You were nothing but insignificant in his gathering. He said: “He is the son of the one who shaved the heads of those whom you see.”

key_terms.التَّوْحِيدِ: tawḥīd, the doctrine of divine unity
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْجَبْرِ: compulsion or predestination in theological discourse
key_terms.الْقَدَرِ: divine decree or determination as discussed in theological debate
key_terms.الْمَجَالِسَ: gatherings or assemblies, described here as a trust
key_terms.حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ: the jugular vein, expressing extreme nearness
key_terms.غُفْرَانِهِ: His forgiveness, to which the House is described as a path
key_terms.قِبْلَةً: the direction of worship for those who perform salat

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام answer objections about the Kaʿbah, hajj, and Allah’s nearness?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a debate in which Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام answers Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ’s objections to the Kaʿbah, hajj, and the reality of Allah’s nearness. The Imam explains that the House is a divine test of obedience and a place of worship, and he affirms Allah’s encompassing knowledge and presence without limitation by place.
